title: bendlang/bend: a language that tries to reject an agent's unproven code
friendlyTitle: Bend tries to reject agent-written code that cannot meet a proof
summary: Bend 2 is an Apache-2.0 language whose pitch is that a proof check blocks code, including code an agent writes, when it does not meet the stated laws. Version 2.0.39 landed on 23 October. The project says the compiler is mostly AI-written and not fully audited, and that the checker itself is not proven. A separate `--verdict` path uses a proven kernel on the translated terms. GitHub's daily TypeScript trending list had it at 113 stars today. The repository has 24,109 stars.
friendlySummary: Bend 2 is a programming language whose pitch is that a proof check blocks code, including code an agent writes, when it does not meet the stated rules. Version 2.0.39 landed on 23 October. The project says the compiler is mostly AI-written and not fully audited, and that the checker itself is not proven. A separate `--verdict` path uses a proven kernel on the translated terms. GitHub's daily TypeScript trending list had it at 113 stars today. The repository has 24,109 stars. The license is Apache-2.0.
whyItMatters: If an agent is generating programs and you want a machine check instead of a hopeful test run, Bend is a place to put the laws in the language. It is not a guarantee that the program on your machine is safe. The project says backends can still differ, the parser is not proven, and the language is young. Treat a green check as a check of the terms it actually saw.
